purpose: Prepare a formal Taiwan human-research ethics/IRB applicability determination packet for the frozen Calibration v13 design without self-declaring exemption, expedited review, approval, or collection authority.

primaryLaw.name: Human Subjects Research Act / 人體研究法

relevantArticles.reason: Defines human-subjects research to include acquisition, investigation, analysis, or use of personal biological, behavioral, physiological, psychological, genetic, medical, or related information.
Requires research-plan ethics review before implementation unless the study falls within an officially announced exemption scope.
Lists required protocol contents including investigator/institution, summary, participants/methods, consent, resources, funding, expected benefits, result ownership/use, and conflicts.
Researchers not affiliated with a research institution may obtain review from a research-institution IRB or an independent IRB.
Requires participant consent in the form and content approved by the review board unless an official waiver applies.

Requires understandable disclosure of institution/funding, purpose/method, investigator/contact, rights/data protection, withdrawal, foreseeable risks/remedies, retention/use, and possible commercial interests.
Addresses destruction of research materials after study end or retention expiry, subject to consent or delinking exceptions.

expeditedReview.name: 倫理審查委員會得簡易程序審查之人體研究案件範圍
expeditedReview.relevance: Includes some minimal-risk studies of individual/group characteristics or behavior, but applicability is for IRB/REC determination; this project does not self-classify.

exemption.name: 得免倫理審查委員會審查之人體研究案件範圍
exemption.relevance: Contains limited exemption categories. This packet does not assert that the project qualifies and requests formal determination instead.

qualifiedReviewBoards.name: 衛生福利部人體研究倫理審查委員會查核合格名單
qualifiedReviewBoards.relevance: Use a currently qualified review board or independent board appropriate to the investigator/institution relationship.

basis: age, sex-for-weighting, macro-region, and household-registration eligibility used for psychometric/fairness/norming analyses
workingClassification.requestedDetermination: IRB/REC to determine review applicability and review category
workingClassification.reasonNotToSelfClassify: The study concerns cognitive ability and subgroup fairness/norming analyses; the review board should determine whether expedited or exempt pathways are appropriate.

studySummary.targetPopulation: Taiwan household-registered adults age 18-65 who can independently read Traditional Chinese and complete the browser-based assessment.
studySummary.studyType: prospective noninterventional online psychometric validation and later representative norming framework
researchTasks: optional six-domain anchor block under separate opt-in where applicable
later independent norming cohort only after separate Phase B readiness and authorization

foreseeableRisks: privacy/confidentiality risk from participant-level research records
psychological discomfort or self-evaluation distress related to cognitive performance
misinterpretation of CPI as IQ despite explicit disclosure
fairness/discrimination concerns if subgroup findings are misused or overgeneralized
mitigations: no name, email, account ID, phone, date of birth, IP address, precise location, street address, or raw county/city storage
whole-year age plus coarse session-level weighting fields only
not-stated option for sex-for-weighting and macro-region
no inference of refused demographic fields from other signals
CPI explicitly not presented as IQ
participant-level raw data prohibited from Git/public artifacts
collection stop rules for privacy incident, schema drift, consent drift, ethics drift, and benchmark expiry

questionsForReviewBoard: Does the planned Calibration v13 study fall within the Human Subjects Research Act as human-subjects research?
If yes, what review category is appropriate: general review, expedited review, exempt-with-certificate, or another pathway?
Can Phase A validation and later Phase B independent norming be covered under one approved protocol with a preregistered amendment gate, or should Phase B require a separate application/amendment?
Are the proposed consent disclosures and not-stated demographic options acceptable?
Is the proposed five-year participant-level retention period acceptable, or should the board require a different period?
Are pseudonymous sourceKey/sessionId plus a short-lived salted recruitment-token hash acceptable for privacy-preserving duplicate control?
Does the board require any additional participant contact, injury/remedy, complaint, or data-controller language for this minimal-risk online study?
Does the board require exclusion or special handling of any protected/vulnerable populations beyond the current adult 18-65 scope?
